report.answer_text:
Cause
The outage began in AWS's US-EAST-1 region (Northern Virginia) late on October 19 Pacific time and ran into October 20, 2025. AWS's post-incident report found the root cause was a latent race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management system.[1]
How the system works: DynamoDB's DNS records are maintained by an automated system with two roles: a DNS Planner that generates new plans, and DNS Enactors that apply them.[2]
What went wrong: Two DNS Enactor processes ran concurrently, and a stale plan check let an old plan overwrite a newer one. Cleanup automation then deleted that plan, wiping all of DynamoDB's DNS records.[3]
Result: The race condition left an empty DNS record for the regional endpoint (dynamodb.us-east-1.amazonaws.com), and the automation failed to repair it.[4] With no IP addresses behind that name, every client lost its connection, including AWS's own internal services.[5]
Why it lasted so long
DynamoDB itself was impaired for about three hours, but the damage spread. The three-hour DynamoDB outage triggered cascading failures in dependent systems, and these effects persisted after DynamoDB connectivity was restored.[1] The failure cascaded across core services such as EC2, Lambda, NLB, ECS/EKS, and dozens of downstream services.[6] Overall, the disruption lasted more than 14 hours.[6]
AWS's response included disabling the DynamoDB DNS Planner and DNS Enactor automation worldwide.[4] For NLB, AWS is adding a velocity control mechanism to limit how much capacity a single NLB can remove when health check failures trigger AZ failover.[4] Early on, AWS said the outage was likely "not" a cyberattack.[7]
What it disrupted
Social and messaging: Snapchat and Reddit were hit.[8] Pinterest users also reported issues.[8]
Gaming: Fortnite, Roblox, Clash Royale and Clash of Clans were among the games that went down.[8]
Finance: Coinbase and Robinhood attributed their outages to AWS.[8] Venmo and Chime also had problems.[8] UK banks such as Lloyds and Halifax showed spikes in reports too.[9]
Amazon's own services: Amazon's shopping site, Prime Video, and Alexa all had issues.[8] As of 1:15 PM ET on October 20, asking Alexa for the weather or to turn off lights still didn't work.[10] Ring was also affected.
Other services: Reports also named Duolingo, Canva, Zoom-adjacent tools, Life360, McDonald's app, Wordle and others.[11] In the UK, government websites were affected.[11]
Scale: Downdetector reported more than 11 million reports of connectivity issues, with over 2,500 companies seeing increased reports.[7] Amazon announced by 6:53 PM ET on October 20 that it had resolved the "increased error rates and latencies."[10]
